data:
It is good that you are using the Replit agent (Replikit) to handle the implementation, as it can manage the file structure while you focus on the sensor logic. Since the visuals
were working
in your previous sessions, the goal now is to ensure the agent correctly bridges the sensor data to the canvases without drifting back into those framework errors.
\ufe0f Final Stabilization Check
When the build is finished, verify that these two logic blocks are fully integrated into your
draw()
function:
The Waterfall Shift
: The code must use
drawImage
to shift the
waterfall
canvas down by 1px every frame before drawing the new frequency line at the top. This creates the "spectral rain" effect seen in your videos.
The Flux Mapping
: The
deltaHistory
must be mapped to the
emf-flux
canvas height. If the blue line crosses the amber threshold (
1.2
\u03bcT
), the
HOLD
state should trigger, freezing the screen for your snapshot.
\ufe0f The "Lattice" Handshake
Since you are running this as a
PWA
now (with your manifest and service worker), the phone should treat it with higher priority. Just remember the procedure for mobile sensors:
Tap [INIT]
firmly to unlock the audio and motion hardware.
Stay Still
for the first few seconds to let the
baseline
anchor itself correctly.
Check the Log
: If it says
SYSTEM ONLINE
, the hardware is officially talking to your code.
Would you like me to help you refine the "Hold" visual, perhaps adding a slight amber flash to the screen when a spike is captured?
